summary: Cold read of docs/specs/ask-reopen-saved-report.md. Six findings, and the sharpest is a security one the spec had actively got wrong: it required a refused reopen to KEEP the previous answer, which contradicts decision 0028 - a revoked grant must produce a refusal, not a cached figure - and continueTurn preserves the old response on every failure, so a revoked user would go on reading numbers they may no longer see. The read also showed the spec's scroll and pending promises are unreachable under the current navigation order, since both entry points await the whole re-run before navigating to Ask, and that continueTurn's failure copy is period-specific for every non-success - so the spec's 'no change to continueTurn' clause could not stand. Two questions went to the human: how a refusal should treat the stale answer, and whether to navigate before running.
gaps: Turn identity was undefined: Selection carries ordered arrays, filters, optional timeWindow fields and limit, and the spec said neither structural nor semantic equality, nor which turns are even eligible candidates, nor which wins when the user has manually created two turns with that selection.

The re-run's question and audit text was unspecified. Both open paths pass selectionLabel(selection).title - only the measure names - while continueTurn displays the turn's own question but SENDS the question it is given, so a naive implementation would display the user's wording and audit 'Actual · Budget'.

The 'previous answer stays visible' and scroll promises could not happen under the current navigation order: pinned-reports.tsx:67 and saved-views.tsx:64 both AWAIT the whole re-run before router.push('/ask'), so there is no Ask panel on screen while it runs and a slow click still looks inert.

The stated continuation capability was inaccurate and self-contradictory: continueTurn discards the server's refusal and shows period-specific copy ('That period could not be loaded. Choose a period to try again.') for ANY typed non-success and for transport failures alike, so it can neither explain why a saved report was refused nor support an authorization distinction - while the spec declared its failure behaviour out of scope.

The grill brief's already-answered ledger cites accepted decisions 0035 and 0036, but the active corpus ends at 0029, and it describes ask-period-control as unplanned although the roadmap records it done.
contradictions: The spec required a refused reopen to retain the previous answer, which contradicts accepted decision 0028: a revoked grant must produce a refusal rather than a cached figure. continueTurn preserves the old response on every failure, so a user whose access had been revoked would keep reading numbers they may no longer see.
resolutions: Behaviour now defines candidates (successful turns carrying response.selection), structural comparison over the RESOLVED selection the server returned - so a pin saved before a period was normalised still matches its own answer - and a deterministic winner when several match: the most recent. Criteria 1-3 pin all three.
Criterion 4 requires a matched turn to re-run with turn.question and the REQUEST BODY to be asserted rather than inferred, and states that a new turn uses the label because no better text exists.

HUMAN ROUND 2: navigate to Ask FIRST, then run. The click gets an instant visible effect, and the pending state and scroll become observable at all. Criterion 6 requires navigation before the request completes.

HUMAN ROUND 1: an authorization or policy refusal CLEARS the stale result and shows why; a transport failure keeps it. The spec now states plainly that this changes continueTurn's failure handling - which an earlier draft wrongly placed out of scope - and that its period-specific copy must become a message that fits the reason. Its pending and replacement-on-success semantics stay as shipped.
The stale ledger assertions are recorded in Out of scope as stale and corrected rather than treated as constraints: the decision corpus ends at 0029 and ask-period-control is done.

CONTRADICTION with decision 0028 resolved by HUMAN ROUND 1 rather than by amending 0028: an authorization or policy refusal now CLEARS the stale result and shows why, so a revoked grant yields a refusal and not a cached figure, exactly as 0028 requires. A transport failure keeps the answer, because nothing has said the user may not see it. Criterion 7 proves the two separately.

rounds.question: The grill found a leak. `continueTurn` keeps the previous answer visible on ANY failure. So if your access to that data has been revoked, reopening a pin shows a refusal message with the old numbers still on screen underneath — decision 0028 says a revoked grant must produce a refusal, not a cached figure. How should a refused reopen behave?
options: Keep it visible for every failure

rounds.question: Both Dashboard and Explore currently await the whole re-run BEFORE navigating to Ask, so you sit on the old page with no feedback and only then jump. That also makes 'the previous answer stays visible' and 'scroll to it' impossible — there's no Ask panel on screen yet. What should a click do?
